name: Maritime
title: Port call readiness and exception coordination
summary: Reconcile vessel arrival estimates, berth constraints, cargo readiness, and agency documents for port-operator decisions.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A shipping line prepares a port call while arrival estimates, terminal readiness, pilot availability, and cargo documents change independently. Operations staff need a coherent readiness picture. Agents support coordination and document checks; masters, pilots, terminal operators, and authorized officials retain navigation and clearance authority.
problem: Estimated arrival is not a berthing commitment, and a complete document packet is not official clearance. Conflicting timezones and late cargo updates can make a schedule appear feasible when an essential service remains unconfirmed.
whyAgents: Arrival, terminal, document, and service-coordination specialists inspect separate interfaces. A durable port-call workflow tracks dependencies and authoritative acknowledgements without granting agents control over navigation or official declarations.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure coordination clarity and unresolved dependency age alongside port-call performance. Berthing and cargo outcomes depend on physical operations and authorized decisions; a complete agent packet does not itself establish operational or regulatory readiness.

agents.name: Arrival evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Compare authenticated vessel updates and estimated arrival revisions.
agents.boundary: Cannot navigate, issue sailing instructions, or treat estimates as confirmed arrival.

agents.name: Terminal readiness agent
agents.responsibility: Check berth plans, cargo readiness, and handling constraints.
agents.boundary: Cannot assign berths or override terminal restrictions.

agents.name: Document completeness agent
agents.responsibility: Compare supplied agency documents with the configured port-call checklist.
agents.boundary: Cannot declare customs clearance or sign official submissions.

agents.name: Service coordination agent
agents.responsibility: Draft pilot, tug, and agency coordination requests with dependencies.
agents.boundary: Authorized operators approve bookings and external communications.

systems.name: Vessel and port-call systems
systems.role: Provide voyage identity, event timestamps, and source-owned arrival estimates.

systems.name: Terminal and service platforms
systems.role: Own berth allocations, cargo operations, pilot or tug confirmations, and local constraints.

systems.name: Agency document workspace
systems.role: Retains submitted documents, official acknowledgement references, and authorized correspondence.

flow.title: Open port-call case
flow.description: Bind vessel, voyage, port, terminal, and responsible operator using governed identifiers and explicit timezones.

flow.title: Reconcile arrival evidence
flow.description: Compare estimate revisions and report age; retain uncertainty instead of converting a predicted time into a commitment.

flow.title: Gather readiness constraints
flow.description: Retrieve berth, cargo, pilot, tug, and agency dependencies from their authoritative owners.

flow.title: Check documentation
flow.description: Apply the configured document checklist and distinguish submitted, accepted, rejected, and pending official states.

flow.title: Prepare coordination options
flow.description: Show operators feasible sequences and unresolved confirmations without proposing navigational or clearance decisions.

flow.title: Record approved coordination
flow.description: Submit authorized booking or document requests with stable keys and track each external acknowledgement before declaring readiness.

diagrams.title: Failure and decision sequence
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Vessel and port-call systems"
    participant H as "Accountable reviewer"
O->>S: Read port-call and document status
    S-->>O: Documents submitted but acceptance pending
    O->>H: Present unresolved official dependency
    H-->>O: Approve agency follow-up
    O->>S: Track acceptance reference separately
diagrams.caption: A local-time berth window is interpreted as UTC. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A local-time berth window is interpreted as UTC.
failures.detection: Timezone validation conflicts with terminal metadata and service booking intervals.
failures.recovery: Block the schedule, normalize times with source timezone, and request operator review of affected bookings.

failures.scenario: Documents are submitted but official acceptance is pending.
failures.detection: Acknowledgement state lacks a valid acceptance reference.
failures.recovery: Keep clearance pending and route follow-up to the authorized agent instead of reporting the vessel cleared.

controls: Keep navigation, vessel safety, and official clearance decisions outside agent authority.
Attach timezone, source, and revision to every arrival and service-window timestamp.
Distinguish document completeness from submission and official acceptance.
Require operator approval for pilot, tug, berth-related requests, and agency correspondence.
Track service reservations and release expired options to avoid conflicting bookings.

metrics.name: Readiness packet latency
metrics.definition: Time from port-call update to operator-reviewable dependency and document status.

metrics.name: Confirmation completeness
metrics.definition: Required services with current authoritative acknowledgements divided by required services for the approved plan.

metrics.name: Timestamp consistency
metrics.definition: Audited schedule events with correct timezone and source revision divided by audited events.

metrics.name: Pending dependency age
metrics.definition: Elapsed time of each unresolved readiness dependency, reported by owning organization.

tradeoffs.cost: Source owners may update at different cadences.
Operators must manage more intermediate workflow states.
Frequent changes can cause reservation churn and repeated review.

rollout.acceptance: Operators validate timezone handling, document states, and conflicting service confirmations.
One port route evaluates readiness packets without bookings or official submissions.
Selected service requests launch after pending-clearance and changed-arrival exercises pass.
